identified_problem: Cyrela is one of Brazil's largest residential real estate developers, with a portfolio of high-end and middle-income projects across São Paulo and other major cities. The April-May 2024 floods in Rio Grande do Sul and recurring urban flash floods in São Paulo and coastal cities directly threaten construction sites, inventory and delivered assets.
climate_exposure: The company owns, develops and sells residential properties concentrated in Brazilian metropolitan areas exposed to flooding, landslides and heat stress.
potential_pain: Climate-driven construction delays, asset damage and buyer-risk perception are hard to quantify and mitigate without location-specific flood and wildfire exposure data.
evidence: Per-project flood and wildfire exposure screening with historical event intelligence for Cyrela's development pipeline.
recommended_message: Show how Talaix can screen flood and wildfire exposure across Cyrela's development pipeline to inform site selection, insurance and buyer due diligence.
fit_score: Major national residential developer with a nationwide project portfolio; direct physical asset exposure to Brazil's 2024 floods and recurring urban flooding makes climate risk intelligence highly relevant.
